subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Right to Protest Anonymously
description: A fast breakdown of The Right to Protest Anonymously for builders.

hook.text: Hong Kong protesters wore masks and used laser pointers to blind surveillance cameras.

buildup.text: Anonymity at protests protects people from government retaliation, firing, or arrest.

discovery.text: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in 1995 that anonymous speech is protected by the First Amendment.

twist.text: Facial recognition makes protest anonymity nearly impossible. A photo can identify you later.

climax.text: The right to protest only works if people aren't afraid. Surveillance makes everyone afraid.

punchline.text: No anonymity, no protest. Fear wins.

quiz.question: Why is anonymity important for the right to protest?
options: It protects protesters from government retaliation
It allows people to commit crimes
It makes protests more effective at recruiting
